subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add public lane-routing semantics for browser/workload/channel isolation, and should that contract be browser-only, per-channel, per-agent, workload-classified, or priority-based?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix adds public scheduler/config semantics and must settle compatibility, resource caps, trust boundaries, and overlap with adjacent lane proposals.

options.title: Design unified scheduler lanes
options.body: Add one maintainer-owned lane classification model covering slow workloads and channel or agent isolation while preserving an aggregate safety cap.

options.title: Narrow to browser isolation
options.body: Add a smaller browser-workload lane only if maintainers want browser automation to be the sole special case for now.

options.title: Fold into per-agent scheduler work
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 as the broader design vehicle and keep this issue as browser/workload evidence.

recommendation.title: Design unified scheduler lanes
recommendation.body: Add one maintainer-owned lane classification model covering slow workloads and channel or agent isolation while preserving an aggregate safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans lane resolution, gateway lane setup, and queue documentation that define the scheduler product surface.
